name: integer-functions-v1
description: Follow-up hypothesis from the mixed workload. Three new integer functions and held-out vectors. The original 100% acceptance threshold is retained.

discovery.task: Write only a Python function named inc returning its argument plus one.

evidence.text: The calling interface accepts and returns integers.
The calling interface accepts and returns integers.

cases.task: Write only a Python function named square that returns its integer argument multiplied by itself. Use one return statement.

evidence.text: The interface accepts one integer and returns one integer. The input may have either sign.
The interface accepts one integer and returns one integer. The input may have either sign.

cases.task: Write only a Python function named subtract that returns its first integer argument minus its second. Use one return statement.

evidence.text: The interface takes two integers and returns one integer. Preserve the order of the supplied arguments.
The interface takes two integers and returns one integer. Preserve the order of the supplied arguments.

cases.task: Write only a Python function named triple that returns its integer argument multiplied by 3. Use one return statement.

evidence.text: The caller supplies a signed integer. The return value must be an integer for both positive and negative inputs.
The caller supplies a signed integer. The return value must be an integer for both positive and negative inputs.
